title: Snapshot reindex and trace-gap recovery for customer dashboards
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Several customers (hosted + Dedicated + Private tenants) reported missing time-series on Console dashboards and broken trace links during a multi-region deployment last night. Symptoms: dashboard panels returned 0-series for recent 30m windows, live query errors (504/empty payload) for metric-store reads, and trace UI showed 'missing span index' for many request IDs. Impacted features: cost/latency panels, rollout health graphs, and per-tenant trace drilldowns. Business impact: multiple enterprise customers raised escalations; two Dedicated customers opened support tickets requesting immediate remediation and data recovery.

Initial triage found a correlated spike in metrics-indexer restart churn coincident with a schema migration to the metrics service (migration M2026-03-01-03). The migration included a column rename and compaction task which caused the indexer to evict in-memory anchors and temporarily drop write forwarding to the rehydration queue for certain tenant namespaces (affecting both hosted and Private-forwarded collectors). Additionally the trace-relay microservice had a rollback to an older protobuf schema in the same window which produced mismatches for trace->metric link IDs, causing the UI to surface broken relinked spans.

Work completed so far: hotfix 1 (metrics-indexer): reverted the compaction flag and deployed metrics-indexer v1.12.4-hotfix to all regions (hosted + dedicated pools). Hotfix 2 (trace-relay): deployed trace-relay v0.9.7 which restores compatible protobuf mapping. Started a targeted backfill job to reindex snapshots for the impacted tenant namespaces and a manual rehydration for dashboard materialized views.

Remaining scope: monitor backfill progress, validate dashboard panels across representative customer tenants, and reconcile any remaining orphaned metric-series. Postmortem actions include adding a pre-migration check to detect in-flight rehydration queues, adding an end-to-end regression test (ingest->index->dashboard->trace link) in CI, and revising the migration runbook to require a canary region and a staged compaction window.

Expected outcome: full visibility restored for affected dashboards, trace links relinked for recent 72 hours, and improved guardrails to prevent recurrence.
